name: work-mode-registry
purpose: Defines selectable work modes so the workspace can avoid running the full governance loop for every task while preserving stronger review for durable, risky, or research-heavy work.

reader_guide.summary: Choose a work mode after web-first intake and memory bootstrap. The selected mode controls which artifacts are blocking before close-out and which improvements may be deferred.
how_to_read: Read default_mode first to know the fallback when the user does not choose a mode.
Read modes to pick the lightest mode that still fits the work risk.
Read mode_enforcement to understand which parts are prompt guidance and which parts are deterministic gates.
Read evaluator_policy to understand which target fields are blocking in each mode.
Read deferred_improvement_rules before using ship_first or postponing improvement work.
update_triggers: The user asks to change the work loop, close-out strictness, or improvement timing.
A repeated task feels too slow because it runs unnecessary requirements, specs, or history steps.
A repeated task feels too slow because independent lanes could run in parallel.
The user asks to make modes enforceable instead of prompt-only.
The user asks to prevent omissions or require explicit task coverage checks.
The user asks to prevent memory leaks or other runtime resource leaks.
A new workflow type needs a different risk tier.

structure_rules.rule: Every mode still starts with web-first intake unless it is unavailable or irrelevant and that exception is recorded.
structure_rules.reason: The user made web-first intake a durable rule; work modes reduce governance overhead, not source grounding.

structure_rules.rule: Use the lightest mode that covers risk, durability, and user intent; do not run governance artifacts only because they exist.
structure_rules.reason: The user asked to avoid running every loop for every task.

structure_rules.rule: In ship_first mode, implementation and verification may happen before requirements/spec backfill, but explicit improvement ideas must point to deferred_improvement_targets.
structure_rules.reason: Deferred work should be visible and reviewable instead of forgotten.

structure_rules.rule: Use governance mode for durable rules, platform structure, evaluation policy, memory anchors, source registries, and other cross-workspace behavior.
structure_rules.reason: High-blast-radius changes need the existing full loop.

structure_rules.rule: Parallel execution does not replace work mode selection; first choose the lightest sufficient mode, then use parallel-work-planner-agent when speed or independent lanes matter. Multiple parallel research lanes must have a merge gate before downstream implementation.
structure_rules.reason: The user wants faster work without losing dependency, conflict, coordination, and final verification controls.

structure_rules.rule: A work mode described only in a prompt is advisory. Enforceable modes must be represented in this registry, checked by the work-mode CLI, recorded in a mode selection artifact, and blocked by the evaluator when required fields are missing.
structure_rules.reason: The user noted that prompt-only modes increase freedom but do not make the platform design robust.

structure_rules.rule: Non-quick work must leave an omission_check_targets record that maps required user instructions, requirements, artifacts, and acceptance checks to evidence, deferral, or not-applicable rationale.
structure_rules.reason: The user noted that an agent can miss something; omissions should be caught by an explicit close-out gate instead of relying on memory.

structure_rules.rule: When a task touches long-running agents, servers, browser automation, workers, subprocesses, caches, streams, large-data processing, file handles, network connections, timers, or subscriptions, it must set resource_risk_occurred=true and leave resource_check_targets with lifecycle, cleanup, and memory measurement evidence.
structure_rules.reason: The user noted that this kind of platform must be careful about memory leaks; runtime resource leaks should be handled by a gate, not a reminder.

field_guide.meaning: Machine-checkable enforcement layers that make work modes stronger than prompt guidance.
Fallback work mode when the user does not explicitly choose one.
Selectable modes with intent, examples, required artifacts, and deferred artifacts.
Rules for selecting a mode from user intent and risk.
Mapping between work modes and blocking work-evaluator target fields.
Rules for recording non-blocking improvement work that should happen later.

mode_enforcement.principle: Prompt instructions are advisory; durable work modes become reliable only when a deterministic gate checks registry shape, mode selection records, evaluator policy, and final reports.

layers.purpose: Keep mode definitions, intended use, required artifacts, and evaluator target fields in one self-documenting JSON file.
Block drift between registry modes and the Python evaluator's required target policy.
Require standard, ship_first, research, and governance work to leave a mode selection record with reason, overrides, and enforcement checks.
Require non-quick work to prove required items, outputs, and acceptance checks were explicitly covered or consciously deferred.
layers.enforced_by: omission_check_targets in evaluate-work input, backed by PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m agent_platform.cli check-omissions <input.json>

layers.purpose: Require runtime-risk work to prove memory and resource lifecycle cleanup, bounded growth, and measurement or rationale before close-out.
layers.enforced_by: resource_check_targets in evaluate-work input when resource_risk_occurred=true, backed by PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m agent_platform.cli check-resources <input.json>

layers.purpose: Turn missing mode-required artifacts into blocking close-out gaps.
Persist the final enforcement result so future agents can audit the mode decision and close-out state.

non_goals: Do not remove agent judgment; enforce the minimum gates that protect platform integrity.
Do not force full governance for quick, tiny, reversible work unless another rule makes it mandatory.

modes.label: Quick
modes.intent: Small, low-risk, reversible work where full requirements/spec/history backfill would cost more than the change.
use_when: read-only answer or tiny doc correction
avoid_when: source code behavior changes with user impact
external factual recommendations with high stakes
modes.closeout_gate: evaluate-work still checks initial instruction, result summary, changed files, and verification; full governance targets are advisory unless another rule makes them mandatory.

modes.label: Standard
modes.intent: Default mode for meaningful but not emergency work. Keeps the established close-out loop.
avoid_when: urgent patch where backfill should happen after verification
pure research capture with no implementation
modes.closeout_gate: evaluate-work blocks close-out when any standard required target, including mode_selection_record_targets and omission_check_targets, is missing.

modes.label: Ship First
modes.intent: Deliver or repair first, then defer non-blocking improvement work into a visible backlog.
use_when: the user wants a fast working result
requirements/spec backfill would slow a small urgent fix
avoid_when: governance, safety, or source registry changes
unknown risk or unclear acceptance criteria
work that cannot be verified immediately
modes.closeout_gate: evaluate-work blocks close-out on references_checked, mode_selection_record_targets, omission_check_targets, web_search_record_targets, and deferred_improvement_targets when improvement ideas exist.

modes.label: Research
modes.intent: Broad source collection, evidence synthesis, or planning where source provenance matters more than implementation artifacts.
avoid_when: source code implementation is already selected
modes.closeout_gate: evaluate-work blocks close-out on research evidence, source provenance, mode selection record, omission coverage, web search record, and timing summary.

modes.label: Governance
modes.intent: High-blast-radius changes to durable rules, workflows, evaluators, memory anchors, platform behavior, source registries, or requirements.
use_when: evaluator, memory, requirement, spec, or source registry behavior changes
new cross-project platform capability is added
modes.closeout_gate: evaluate-work blocks close-out when any governance required target, including mode_selection_record_targets and omission_check_targets, is missing.

selection_rules: If the user explicitly selects a mode, use that mode unless it conflicts with safety or repository rules; record any override.

If no mode is selected, classify from risk and durability: quick for tiny reversible work, research for evidence synthesis, ship_first for verified urgent delivery, governance for durable platform/rule changes, otherwise standard.
When uncertain between two modes, choose the stronger mode only for real risk, durability, or cross-project impact.
If speed matters and independent lanes exist, keep the selected work_mode and add a parallel-work plan instead of inventing a new mode.
For every non-quick mode, create or update a mode selection record and include it in mode_selection_record_targets before close-out.
For every non-quick mode, create or update an omission check record and include it in omission_check_targets before close-out.
When runtime resource risk exists in any mode, create or update a resource leak check record and include it in resource_check_targets before close-out.
Mode selection does not remove the requirement to avoid unsupported factual claims.
deferred_improvement_rules: Use _ops/backlog/deferred-improvements.ko.md and .en.md for shared deferred improvements.
Project-specific deferred improvements belong in the owning project's backlog or docs area.
A deferred improvement must record why it was deferred, owner scope, trigger to revisit, and related artifacts.
Do not defer known blocking gaps, failed verification, or unsupported factual claims.
